question: Does the pinned realFluidReactingFoam build run at all on a correctly configured case, and what is the smallest defensible set of case changes required to exercise its intended equations?
conclusion: Two per-species div-scheme entries in fvSchemes resolved the observed startup failure, and the target solver then integrated 200 time steps to the requested endTime with the Peng-Robinson property path and a normal End. This establishes that the startup failure was caused by missing discretization entries; it does not rule out defects elsewhere, and it does not establish that these are the only changes a full reacting case would need.

environment.note: The container cannot run the host-built solver (libmpi.so.40 absent), so both arms executed on the host under the profile env file, as in cfd-job-001.

armA-as-shipped.change: none; the case as shipped, which specifies application reactingFoam
armA-as-shipped.outcome: FOAM FATAL IO ERROR: keyword div(((hei_O2*rho)*YVi_O2)) is undefined in .../system/fvSchemes/divSchemes

armB-with-species-schemes.change: two lines added to divSchemes, see changes/fvSchemes.diff
armB-with-species-schemes.outcome: normal End; 200 time steps; last reported time 0.002 equals the requested endTime

comparison.baseline: the package's own reactingFoam build on the same case, cfd-job-001
comparison.note: First-and-last sampled values, not a time history. The 0.06 K difference at max T is in the direction and rough magnitude expected of the extra species-diffusion enthalpy flux terms that realFluidReactingFoam carries and reactingFoam does not; it is not here established to be that term, only that the two solvers do not diverge over 200 steps.

hypotheses.H1_missing_discretization_entries: supported for this case and window — adding the entries was sufficient to complete the interval
hypotheses.H2_needs_more_case_structure: not supported — no further case change was required to complete this interval
hypotheses.implementation_defect: not observed over this window, but not excluded elsewhere; a short reaction-free interval is weak evidence about the reacting path
hypotheses.temperature_difference_attribution: not established — the 0.06 K gap is observed only as two scalar extrema, and the two solvers differ in three coupled places, so it is not attributed to any single term

reviewer_caveats: min/max(T) values are the last sampled line of each log, not a history, and cannot bound the field over the run
the solver's own term 'time step continuity errors' is recorded as such and is not read as a linear-solver residual or a proof of convergence
200 steps at deltaT 1e-5 to endTime 0.002 is a short window; it establishes that the equations can be exercised, not that the case is physically correct
the 0.06 K agreement is a single sampled comparison against one baseline run, not a statistic and not a validation

the direction and magnitude of the temperature difference are not established as the expected effect of any particular term; the two solvers differ in three coupled places and only two scalar extrema are compared
this case has no chemical reaction; nothing here speaks to the reacting path or to the MASCOTTE flame
